newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: After an initial bout of excitement which saw the market strengthen as foreign banks bought stock and institutions nibbled, long bonds spent most of the day drifting to end only slightly stronger.
At 1415 GMT the key R150 stock was yielding 15.15 percent from 15.18 percent late on Wednesday.

The market started the day unchanged from its overnight levels but traders said buying by foreign banks soon pushed yields down. This was augmented by jobber interest and institutional nibbling at higher levels.

"Technically the market is now looking bullish despite dodgy economic fundamentals," a senior bond trader said, referring to recent worse-that-expected money supply and private sector credit extension and trade numbers.
He said the 15.13 percent level was providing resistance on the downside and would be an important level to watch on Friday.

Preliminary money supply data released on Wednesday showed growth of 15.82 percent in February against a consensus of 15.1 percent while private sector growth came in at 17.34 percent against a consensus 16.39 percent.
Dealers said the higher numbers signalled a delay in prospects for a Bank rate cut although some downplayed negative reaction, saying the figures were not "excessively" bad.
They said it was difficult to pinpoint a clear trend but underlying sentiment was bullish based on technical factors.
Players would be seeking direction from the U.S. market on Friday which was awaiting the release of the March U.S. unemployment report.
Foreigners were net buyers of 289.08 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 330.69 million rand's worth on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 3.99 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.19 billion rand on Tuesday.
The rand maintained a tight range, ending slightly firmer after limited reaction to the money supply data.
"The figure was not good but it was also not excessively bad," a senior forex trader said.
The unit was expected to hold in its established 4.41 to 4.43 range on Friday with players watching the bond market for direction.
"No fireworks...it's looking pretty steady," another trader commented.
Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.2504/2598 versus sterling from 7.2707/2800 and at 0.3772/3775 marks from 0.3777/3782 marks.
Short-term money market rates were quoted steady with three-month deposit rates all at 16.55 percent offered and the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.90 to 16.10 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 10.811 billion rand on Wednesday from 10.414 billion rand on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank said.
